description: Knee fallout guide: lower one bent knee to the side with a still pelvis to train inner thighs and hips. Covers mistakes, easier and harder versions.
intro: Knee fallouts are a gentle lying-down move: one bent knee slowly opens to the side and returns while the pelvis stays steady. They train control of the inner thighs and hips. In a pelvic floor routine they also give a mild inner-thigh stretch and a chance to practice letting the pelvic area relax.
feel: You should feel your lower belly keep the pelvis level and a light stretch or effort along the inner thigh. You should not feel the opposite hip lift, your back arch or your breath stop. Rest your hands on the front of your hip bones: they should stay level as the knee lowers.

mistakes.wrong: Letting the pelvis roll with the knee
mistakes.right: Lower the knee only as far as your hips stay level. A smaller clean range is better.
Lower for about three seconds and return just as slowly.

mistakes.wrong: Clenching the pelvic floor the whole time
mistakes.right: Keep it soft between reps. This move is about control, not constant squeezing.

easier: Put a pillow under the outer thigh so the knee has a short way to go, or do fewer reps.
harder: Pause with the knee halfway out for two breaths, or straighten the other leg along the floor so the pelvis works harder to stay still.
who: Helpful after childbirth once you are cleared to exercise, for anyone wanting a calm evening routine, and for people with tight inner thighs or a pelvic floor that tends to stay tense.
skip: Check with a doctor or pelvic floor physiotherapist first if you have pubic or groin pain, recent pelvic surgery, or pain at the front of the pelvis during or after pregnancy. If the hip pinches, reduce the range. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: Are knee fallouts good after a C-section?
faq.a: They are a common early move because the load is low. Wait until your doctor or midwife says you can start gentle exercise.

faq.q: Should I do a Kegel during knee fallouts?
faq.a: You can add a gentle squeeze as the knee returns, then fully relax. Many people get more from keeping the pelvic floor soft here.
